# Duct

> Duct is an open-source (MIT) AI agent for product and growth teams: see the whole picture, fix it in the same moment. It connects Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Mixpanel, Stripe and eight more tools, reads across all of them at once, finds what needs to change, and changes it when you approve. It remembers what it learns about your business. Desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux, free with your own model keys or a ChatGPT subscription; self-hostable; source at https://github.com/5hirish/duct. This site is published in English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German and Japanese.

Duct is built and maintained by Shirish Kadam in Spain. It answers questions a single dashboard cannot ("why did signups drop last week", "which content converts", "where is the ads budget leaking") by reading the tools together rather than one at a time, and every number in an answer is re-checked by a verification sub-agent before it reaches you.

## Three agents

- [Insights](https://getduct.ai/): Ask a question across ads, analytics and revenue. Duct reads Google Ads, GA4, Stripe and the rest together, names the cause with its sources, writes a brief that is saved and versioned, and proposes the change (pause a campaign, add negatives, track an event). Nothing is applied until a human approves; there is no agent-facing apply tool, the boundary is in code.
- [SEO audit](https://getduct.ai/seo-audit): Paste a URL and Duct crawls the site, reads the technical and content signals, and hands back a scored report: keyword clusters on a position map, page-two opportunities, the topics competitors own, nine category scores and the fixes in order. Free, no account, the front door to the product.
- [Content Studio](https://getduct.ai/for-organic-growth): A plan on a board, a post per card, slides and images generated for each, and one click to publish to TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, Threads, X, Facebook, Pinterest and Bluesky. Results come back onto the card so the next plan learns from the last one.

## How it works

- It reads by default. When it can fix something it prepares a change set, shows a preview and a guardrail check, and waits for approval. Changes can be rolled back.
- It remembers: goals, decisions, conclusions from earlier briefs, per project and per user, with a timeline of what it learned and when.
- Connectors: Google Ads, Google Analytics 4, Search Console, Tag Manager, Meta Ads, Apple Search Ads, OpenAI Ads, Mixpanel, Microsoft Clarity, GrowthBook, Stripe, RevenueCat, HubSpot. Google connects with OAuth, read-only unless more is granted; the rest take a key. Credentials are encrypted at rest and scoped to one project.
- Models: bring your own API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), or sign in with a ChatGPT subscription on the desktop app. Keys live in the OS keychain.
- Pricing: free with your own keys, always. A paid plan later bundles the models so nobody has to hold keys; nothing open today moves behind it.

## Documentation

Fact sheets rendered from the repository's `docs/` folder; the file named on each page is the source, and the page follows it.

- [Duct architecture](https://getduct.ai/docs/architecture): An interactive map of the Duct monorepo: the backend, app, desktop shell and site, how they talk to each other, and which file to open first for each job.
- [Data model](https://getduct.ai/docs/data-model): Every table the Duct backend owns, what it records, and which of the four stores answers where something is recorded: rows, events, logs or memories.
- [Agent ports and the event contract](https://getduct.ai/docs/agent-ports-and-events): The harness boundary of Duct's agents: the six ports a runner implements and the server-sent event contract the app renders, and the code that enforces each.
- [Building and changing agents](https://getduct.ai/docs/agent-engineering): How an agent is built and changed in Duct on LangChain, LangGraph and deepagents: the rules, the primitive behind each, what enforces it, and the checklists.
- [Agent output QA — the LLM-as-judge eval harness](https://getduct.ai/docs/agent-evaluation): How Duct tests agents whose output is subjective, a brief or a post, with an LLM-as-judge harness: the trials, the rubric, the judge's biases and mitigations.
- [Credential storage: the local API key and provider auth](https://getduct.ai/docs/credential-storage): Where every secret Duct holds actually lives, on the desktop and on a server: the local API key, provider keys and OAuth tokens, and what protects each of them.
- [Local Security Audit Skill](https://getduct.ai/docs/security-audit-skill-and-hooks): The local security gate for Duct's backend and app: the audit skill, the leak scanner, the pre-commit hook and the policy they enforce before a change ships.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is Duct?**
An open-source AI agent that connects your product, marketing and revenue tools, answers questions across them, proposes changes and applies them when you approve. It runs as a desktop app on macOS, Windows and Linux.

**Is it free?**
Yes. The core is MIT licensed and stays that way. You pay your model provider directly, or sign in with the ChatGPT plan you already have. A hosted team plan comes later; the core stays open.

**Does it change my accounts without asking?**
No. Reporting works with read-only access. A change is proposed with what it touches, and applied only when you press Apply. There is no approve tool in the list the model can call, so it cannot be talked into applying anything. Destructive changes are flagged; anything over a guardrail is blocked until you look.

**Which tools does it connect to?**
Google Ads, Meta Ads, Apple Search Ads, OpenAI Ads, GA4, Search Console, Tag Manager, Mixpanel, Microsoft Clarity, GrowthBook, HubSpot, Stripe and RevenueCat. The four Google tools connect with OAuth; the rest take a read-only key you paste once. Nothing is exported by hand.

**Where do my keys and data live?**
Model keys stay in your operating system's keychain and travel with a request only while a job runs. Connector authorisations are stored encrypted by the hosted API. The desktop app is a thin shell over that API; a self-host build runs everything on your own machine.

**Which models does it use?**
Whichever you bring: an OpenAI, Anthropic or Google API key, or a ChatGPT subscription signed in through the desktop app. Heavy, standard and light tiers can each be pointed at a different model.

**How do I self-host it?**
Clone https://github.com/5hirish/duct and follow the open-source page: the FastAPI backend, the agents and the Next.js app run on your own machine or server, with your own database and keys.

## Open source

- [Duct on GitHub](https://github.com/5hirish/duct): MIT licensed end to end: FastAPI backend, the agents, the Next.js app and a Tauri v2 desktop shell. The downloaded app is a thin shell over the hosted API with model keys in the OS keychain; a self-host build bundles the backend.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/5hirish/duct/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Setup, the checks CI runs, and the conventions. Agent-written contributions are welcome; the PR template asks where an agent helped so a reviewer knows where to look hardest.
- [Discussions](https://github.com/5hirish/duct/discussions): Questions, ideas and design debate.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/5hirish/duct/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
